hardware: GCP g2-standard-48, 4x NVIDIA L4 (23034 MiB each), asia-southeast1-a, Spot

vllm_config.note: transformers pinned to 5.13.1 (wheelhouse version) to avoid AmbiguousGlobalPerLayerAttributeError in 5.20.2

concurrency_scaling.note: 3 trials per level after initial single-trial run showed noisy N=2 result (66%, later confirmed as noise)
concurrency_scaling.verdict: PASS at N=2,3,4 - parallel best-of-N solver design (Design A) is viable on this hardware

per_task_container_a_setup_s.method: swegemma eval --task-id X --max-time-minutes 0.05 --max-tool-calls 1, sandbox=docker; setup_A = wall_A - agent_only_duration_s (task_results.jsonl). Note: the --skip-agent-patch run (phase 2 only) was NOT needed for this subtraction since the near-zero-budget run does not reach phase 2 with an empty patch.

comparison_to_current_configs.T3_7m_7min: 7 x 60 x 120 = 50400s agent-only = 14.0h, OVER budget even before setup
comparison_to_current_configs.conclusion: Every config tested so far (6-8 min caps) exceeds the real 12h ceiling once correctly accounted for. None of our local screens used a scorer-safe cap.

operational_notes: g2-standard-48 (4x L4) Spot and on-demand were stocked out across 14 zones (US, Europe, Asia) at time of attempt; eventually succeeded in asia-southeast1-a via background retry loop.
DLVM image common-cu129-ubuntu-2204-nvidia-580 ships Python 3.10; swegemma requires >=3.12. Installed Python 3.12 via uv (not apt/deadsnakes, which hit a 503 from launchpadcontent.net).
uv venv does not bundle pip; use 'uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python' not 'pip install' after activating.
uv pip resolution of bare 'vllm' package name collided with an unrelated ancient PyPI package (vllm==0.1.2); install the exact wheelhouse .whl file path to avoid this.

PyPI torch resolves to a CUDA 13.0 build by default; the DLVM image ships CUDA 12.9 toolkit. Install torch explicitly from https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu129 first, though vllm's own pinned dependency (torch==2.10.0+cu128) will still override it afterward - this is fine, cu128 is compatible with 12.9 toolkit.

wheelhouse ships transformers 5.13.1; letting pip resolve transformers from PyPI pulls 5.20.2 which raises AmbiguousGlobalPerLayerAttributeError on Gemma 4's per-layer head_dim config. Must pin to the wheelhouse wheel.

First vLLM launch attempt (gpu_memory_utilization=0.90) OOM'd during CUDA graph capture because our L4s report 22.03 GiB usable vs the 24 GB HARNESS_README states - a real ~2GiB/GPU hardware gap. The crashed worker processes leaked ~22.5 GiB per GPU and were not cleaned up automatically; had to kill by PID manually before any retry would work.
Docker was not pre-installed on the DLVM image; installed via get.docker.com.

SSH over IAP to the Spot VM was intermittently flaky (~50% failure rate on any command, unrelated to command content) throughout the session, consistent with behavior seen on other Spot VMs this project - always resolved by retrying 5-10s later.
